rows.why: He put the 'they' ending on 3ind for his own shop's customers; Amal recast عندنا and he repeated it ('عندنا, Oh my god').

rows.amal_said: شو يعني لسه الزباين يروحوا؟ ... لا، لا الزباين يروحوا.
rows.why: He used lissa (sheet: 'still / not yet | Lissa | لسه') for 'until'; Amal asked what he meant and gave لا (until), he asked 'It's just لا?' and she confirmed.
Clock time takes the feminine number; Amal echoed his واحد back, he fixed it ('times are واحدة') and she confirmed الساعة واحدة.

rows.medi_said: Uh, uh, حافز؟ حافز؟ ... لا، أنا نسيت، نسيته، نسيتها.
rows.amal_said: Hafiz is a motivation، بس what's about motivated؟ ... متشـ... متشجع.
rows.why: Amal quizzed him on yesterday's word 'motivated' (sheet: 'motivated | Mitshajje3 | متشجع'); he offered حافز (motivation), said he forgot, and she supplied متشجع.

rows.medi_said: Is it-- Is there a verb for حساب? you guys use it?
rows.why: He asked for the verb 'to consider' and Amal supplied بحسب - a didn't-know.
mitshajje3 takes la- before what you are motivated for - Amal herself had just asked 'متشجع لـ العربي' / 'متشجع إله'; he dropped the preposition and she let it pass (right = my reading).
rows.english: I am motivated for the lesson.

rows.medi_said: أنا فـ، أنا فـ، أنا في الـ Wi-Fi? Is that how you say it?
rows.amal_said: Yeah I'm on the wifi أنا عالـ wifi.
rows.why: 'On the wifi' is 3ala, not fi; Amal recast أنا عالـ wifi and repeated على الـ، عالـ.

rows.medi_said: So Shantet Shogoli, uh, uh, حمرا
rows.why: An adjective on a definite (possessed) noun needs el-; without it it becomes a sentence ('is red') - Amal named it and explained definiteness.

rows.medi_said: So would it be شنتت، شنتت شغلي الأحمر، الأحمر،
rows.why: شنطة is feminine so the colour must be الحمرا; Amal recast it and he repeated الحمراء.

rows.amal_said: ما فيهن means there aren't here ... or there isn't here. ... Yeah, مشون.
rows.why: 'Not here' takes mish, not ma fi (there isn't); Amal explained ma fi means 'there isn't' and confirmed his مش هون.

rows.amal_said: ليش؟ لا، ليش. ... It's اسم or اسم.
rows.why: He added a feminine -t to اسم as the first word of an idafa; اسم is masculine and never takes it - Amal said 'لا، ليش' and 'it can't be a feminine'.
The first word of an idafa never takes el-; he started 'the old name of his school' with الـ اسم and Amal said لا (again at 30:21: 'So it's not الـ اسم' - 'لا').
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.medi_said: So الـ اسم قديم. No, it's like اسم القديمة. Okay, I don't know.
rows.amal_said: لا. [تضحك] لا. ... You just change the gender of Adeem.
rows.why: To make 'old' describe the name, the adjective stays after the whole idafa and takes the gender of اسم (masc): el-2adeem; Amal said لا and told him to change the gender of 2adeem.
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.amal_said: No. Even though in English we don't-- we say the, in Arabic we don't.

rows.amal_said: Mm, it works, yeah. هذا أحسن محل ...
rows.why: محل is masculine so it takes hada not hadi; Amal accepted the sentence ('it works') and only rephrased with هذا (right = my reading).

rows.medi_said: Okay. So أحسن زبون ما، ما ما بتشتري إشي.
rows.why: The sentence was 'the worst customer'; he said أحسن (best) right after saying أسوأ twice - a slip or the engine; Amal's chat has aswa2 and she said nothing (right = my reading).

rows.medi_said: ما ما بتشتري إشي. ما بتشتري. ما بتشتري.
rows.amal_said: It's ما بي، ما بيشتري because it's زبون.
rows.why: The verb must match زبون (masculine, he); Amal recast ما بيشتري 'because it's زبون'.
The verb needs the ending pointing back to حدا; Amal recast بحبه and he said 'There's a pointer'.

rows.why: For 'trip' he said سفر (travel, the verbal noun) instead of سفرة (sheet: '(travel) trip | Safra | سفرة') or رحلة; Amal gave both.

rows.amal_said: Why? ... بس if you say the week's beginning, now you'd have to be إضافة ... It would be the first week.
rows.why: He misread her الأسبوع الأول as 'the beginning of the week'; after the noun with el-, awal is the adjective 'first' - Amal asked why and explained.

rows.medi_said: Il awal il tamreen or il tamreen il awal is the first exercise.
rows.why: awal before the noun never takes el- (Amal said so at 47:59 / 48:38); 'il awal il tamreen' for 'the first exercise' is wrong but she let it pass (right = my reading).

rows.amal_said: Nafs al ishi. ... نفس الـ إشي the same thing. نفس إشي doesn't mean anything.
